reasoning_traces.think:
The calibration framework operates through four distinct yet interrelated constraints: Brier score (resolution + uncertainty), ECE (mean absolute error), Murphy reliability (squared error), and n (sample size). Brier ensures model performance exceeds baseline; ECE isolates miscalibration; Murphy provides a looser but complementary reliability check. Only ECE binds under current conditions, indicating that while other metrics pass, the model's calibration error is narrowly excessive. This reveals a dual nature of calibration: one where resolution and discrimination matter (Brier), and another where alignment with truth matters (ECE). The failure of ECE implies that even if a model performs well on Brier or Murphy, its internal calibration may be misaligned with observed frequencies. The system thus enforces a hierarchy of checks, where ECE acts as the decisive gatekeeper among these four.
